clue.text: During journeys, muse on Conservative dinosaur

indicators.note: something happening during the journeys sits within them, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: journeys are trips

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another follows it, so the muse comes after the party letter

parts.note: Erato is the Muse of love poetry

explanation.surface: Someone muses on Conservative politics while travelling, then a dinosaur turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: The triceratops is a three-horned plant-eating creature of the late Cretaceous, one kind of dinosaur.

clue.text: French head secures drawer maybe, alongside storage unit

indicators.note: a head that secures something holds it fast, so the other pieces go within

parts.note: tête is the French word for head
a drawer is one who draws, such as an RA, a Royal Academician
by means beside or alongside

explanation.surface: A French boss locks a drawer beside some storage furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' suggests furniture, but here it is an artist: RA, a member of the Royal Academy.
explanation.definitionFit: A terabyte is a large measure of computer memory capacity, a unit in which data storage is counted.

clue.text: Current GP with time to treat ordinary skin problem

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: treating something works it over, so these letters are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor finds time to treat an everyday skin complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetigo is a contagious bacterial infection of the skin, producing sores and crusts.

clue.text: Cat returned, tucking into middle of cheese and ham?

indicators.note: the cat tucks itself into the other letters, so it goes inside them
the central pair of letters of the word cheese
returned means the word for the cat is read backwards

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A cat comes back and tucks into a cheese and ham sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' looks like the sandwich filling but is a verb: to overact.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to overact, exaggerating feeling on stage, which is what this verb means; the question mark flags the verb sense.

clue.text: Fruit that's tropical, endlessly cooked

indicators.note: cooked means the letters are worked up into a new arrangement
endlessly means the last letter of tropical is dropped

explanation.surface: A tropical fruit, cooked to destruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' drops the last letter to leave TROPICA, which 'cooked' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The apricot is a soft orange stone fruit, an example of fruit.

clue.text: Legendary Greek newsman, one engrossed in work

indicators.note: being engrossed in something is being absorbed within it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: an opus is a work, especially a musical one
ED is short for editor, a newsman
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A journalist from Greek legend is absorbed in his work.
explanation.definitionFit: Oedipus is the mythical king of Thebes who unknowingly killed his father and married his mother.

clue.text: Lancashire town found, bearing left

parts.note: south is a compass bearing
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A town in Lancashire is located by bearing left.
explanation.definitionFit: Southport is a seaside resort town on the Lancashire coast in north-west England.

clue.text: I don't like three-quarters of novel

indicators.note: taking three-quarters of a four-letter word keeps three letters, losing the last

parts.note: a novel is a book

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes most of a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouting this word is the stock way an audience shows disapproval, the jeer of someone who dislikes it.

clue.text: Expressed approval during relative's dance

indicators.note: something happening during another sits inside it

parts.note: bro is short for brother, a relative
olé is the cheer of approval at a bullfight or flamenco

explanation.surface: Someone cheered while a relative danced.
explanation.definitionFit: The bolero is a lively Spanish dance in triple time, famously set by Ravel.

clue.text: Sharp mint munched in periphery of office

indicators.note: in places the munched letters inside the outer pair
the periphery of a word is its outer letters, first and last
munched means the letters are chewed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A sharp mint is chewed around the edge of the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharp' looks like an adjective for the mint, but it means punctual; 'munched' signals the jumble, 'in' the placing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp, as in 'seven o'clock sharp', means punctually, exactly at the stated hour.

clue.text: Agent bringing round gold copy, shortly

parts.note: a rep, or representative, is an agent

indicators.note: bringing round turns the word for gold back to front

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An agent brings round a gold copy soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' belongs to the definition: the answer is a shortening of reproduction.
explanation.definitionFit: Repro is the clipped form of reproduction, a copy of an original, which 'shortly' signals.

clue.text: School member's ginger hairstyle

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is': the school member is ginger plus a hairstyle

parts.note: red hair is called ginger
a mullet is a hairstyle short at the front and long at the back

explanation.surface: A pupil has ginger hair in a particular cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' is a school of fish, not a place of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish swim in schools, and this red-coloured fish is one member of such a school.

clue.text: Yellow flower, say, seen in black container

indicators.note: seen in places the word for say within the other pieces

parts.note: B is the pencil abbreviation for black
a cup is a container
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A yellow flower is seen in a black pot.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttercup is a common meadow plant of the genus Ranunculus with glossy yellow petals.

clue.text: Group of women are enthralled by leading royal

indicators.note: being enthralled by someone is being held captive by them, so this word sits inside

parts.note: HM, His or Her Majesty, is the leading royal

explanation.surface: A group of women are captivated by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the women of a polygamous household, or their quarters, so a group of women.

clue.text: Brothers, having fast car around, stole aquatic craft

parts.note: TU, a trade union, is a brotherhood, its members brothers

indicators.note: around puts the car's letters round the stole

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, is a fast car
a boa is a feathery stole

explanation.surface: Some brothers with a sports car steal a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' looks like a verb but is a noun, the scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: A tugboat is a small powerful vessel that tows or pushes ships, a craft for the water.

clue.text: Where people are given time over ad-lib, having fluffed line

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: fluffed lines are mangled, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: a ley is a line linking ancient sites

explanation.surface: An actor goes over time, ad-libbing after fluffing a line.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OLD BAILEY is London's Central Criminal Court; 'time' is a prison sentence. 'Having fluffed' jumbles AD-LIB to LDBAI.
explanation.definitionFit: Prison sentences, informally 'time', are handed down at this principal criminal court.

clue.text: Coming back, try starters in motorway services — pea soup?

indicators.note: coming back means these letters are read backwards

parts.note: to have a go is to try

indicators.note: the starters are the opening letters of motorway and services

explanation.surface: On the way back, someone tries the starters at motorway services, including pea soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pea soup' is the old name for thick London fog, not a menu item.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea-souper was a dense yellowish London fog polluted with smoke, the classic thick polluted air.

clue.text: Serviceman once grief-stricken by sound of animal shelter

parts.note: blue means sad, down

indicators.note: sound of means the next word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: a cote is a shelter for doves or sheep

explanation.surface: A soldier is devastated by the sound of an animal shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluecoat was a historical term for a soldier or sailor in a blue uniform, a past serviceman.

clue.text: Appreciative, given mince and almost bursting

parts.note: to grate food is to mince it

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: bursting means full

explanation.surface: Someone is grateful to be given mince when nearly bursting.
explanation.definitionFit: Grateful and appreciative are synonyms, both describing thankfulness.

clue.text: European flower's pronounced smell

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is': the river is the pronounced smell

indicators.note: pronounced means the word is spoken and spelt differently

parts.note: an odour is a smell

explanation.surface: A European bloom has a strong smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is something that flows, a river, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a river in central Europe forming much of the German-Polish border, a flower in crossword terms.

clue.text: Initially read out stirring Auden poem

indicators.note: initially picks the first letters of read and out
stirring means the poet's name is mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone reads aloud a moving poem by Auden.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a short French verse form with a refrain, a kind of poem.

clue.text: Maybe referee part of tennis match, misapplying "let" rule

parts.note: a set is part of a tennis match

indicators.note: misapplying means the letters are used out of order

explanation.surface: A tennis umpire misapplies the let rule during a set.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee settles disputes, so is an example of one who resolves arguments; 'maybe' marks the example.

clue.text: School presses rogue clubs to withdraw from competition

indicators.note: the school presses round the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: a rat is a rogue
C is the card abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A school forces its rogue clubs to pull out of a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull out of a race or contest is to withdraw from it, the sporting sense of the verb.

clue.text: French scientist in the morning training with engineers

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning
PE is physical education, training
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: A French scientist trains with engineers in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: André-Marie Ampère was the French physicist who founded electrodynamics; the unit of current bears his name.

clue.text: Equestrian chore involving stable person

indicators.note: involving means the words contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: A horse-related job involves a stable hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stable' suggests horses, but means steady: someone others rely on.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor is someone who provides steadiness and support to others, a dependable person.

clue.text: Very clever people amend mosaic, keeping central elements

indicators.note: keeping central elements retains only the middle letters of amend and mosaic

explanation.surface: Clever people fix a mosaic while preserving its central tiles.
explanation.definitionFit: Mensa is the society for people with very high IQs.

clue.text: Pointer in animal home thinner than the others

indicators.note: in puts the pointer inside the animal home

parts.note: a nest is home to birds or other animals
an arrow is a pointer

explanation.surface: A pointer dog in an animal shelter is skinnier than the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of narrow: least wide, slimmer than all others.

clue.text: Mark visiting loves Antipodean city

indicators.note: visiting places the mark inside the loves

parts.note: O is love, zero in tennis, here two of them
a tag is a mark or label

explanation.surface: Mark goes to visit his lovers in a southern-hemisphere city.
explanation.walkthrough: Otago is strictly a New Zealand region, not a city, as the blog notes; its main city is Dunedin.
explanation.definitionFit: Otago is in New Zealand's South Island, the Antipodes from a British view; the setter loosely calls it a city.

clue.text: Retired soprano perhaps entertains the ancient king

indicators.note: a host who entertains takes guests in, so the word the goes inside
retired means withdrawn, going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a treble is a high voice, a soprano for example

explanation.surface: A retired soprano hosts an ancient king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' turns TREBLE into ELBERT, which takes in THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethelbert was a king of Kent in the sixth century, the first English king to convert to Christianity.

clue.text: Reserved a turkey from the back

indicators.note: from the back means the word is read starting at its end

parts.note: a turkey is a stupid person, a fool

explanation.surface: Someone stays reserved about a turkey seen from behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloof means distant and cool in manner, synonymous with reserved.

clue.text: Deirdre regularly avoided sin

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the name, here the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Deirdre regularly avoided sinning.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to go wrong morally, a verb meaning to transgress, as in 'to err is human'.

clue.text: Second person to entertain in the large building for itinerants

parts.note: you is the second-person pronoun

indicators.note: in places the entertaining word inside the others

parts.note: to host is to entertain

explanation.surface: A second person comes to entertain in a large hostel for travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth hostel offers cheap lodging to travellers, especially young walkers and backpackers.
